questions.enonce_markdown:
When the polynomial $P(x)$, where $P(x) = 2x^3 + ax^2 + bx - 12$, is divided by $(x+3)$ the remainder is $18$. Given that $(x+1)$ is a factor of $P(x)$,

(a) find the values of the constants $a$ and $b$.

(b) factorise $P(x)$ completely. (9 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a)** By the remainder theorem, dividing $P(x)$ by $(x+3)$ leaves remainder $P(-3)$, so $P(-3) = 18$. By the factor theorem, $(x+1)$ is a factor, so $P(-1) = 0$.

$$
P(-3) = 2(-27) + 9a - 3b - 12 = 9a - 3b - 66 = 18 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 3a - b = 28. \tag{1}
$$

$$
P(-1) = -2 + a - b - 12 = a - b - 14 = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a - b = 14. \tag{2}
$$

Subtracting (2) from (1): $2a = 14$, so $a = 7$. Then from (2): $b = a - 14 = -7$.

Check: $P(x) = 2x^3 + 7x^2 - 7x - 12$, so $P(-3) = -54 + 63 + 21 - 12 = 18$ and $P(-1) = -2 + 7 + 7 - 12 = 0$.

$$\boxed{a = 7,\quad b = -7}$$

**(b)** Since $(x+1)$ is a factor, divide $P(x) = 2x^3 + 7x^2 - 7x - 12$ by $(x+1)$ (synthetic division with root $-1$):

| | $2$ | $7$ | $-7$ | $-12$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $-1$ | | $-2$ | $-5$ | $12$ |
| | $2$ | $5$ | $-12$ | $0$ |

The remainder is $0$ and the quotient is $2x^2 + 5x - 12$. Factorise the quadratic: we need two numbers with product $2 \times (-12) = -24$ and sum $5$, namely $8$ and $-3$:

$$2x^2 + 5x - 12 = 2x^2 + 8x - 3x - 12 = 2x(x+4) - 3(x+4) = (2x-3)(x+4).$$

Hence

$$\boxed{P(x) = (x+1)(2x-3)(x+4)}$$

Check by expansion: $(x+1)(2x^2 + 5x - 12) = 2x^3 + 5x^2 - 12x + 2x^2 + 5x - 12 = 2x^3 + 7x^2 - 7x - 12$. Correct. The roots of $P(x) = 0$ are $x = -4,\ -1,\ \tfrac32$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the set of real values of $k$, for which the roots of the quadratic equation $x^2 + kx + 3 + k = 0$ are real and distinct. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The roots of $x^2 + kx + (3+k) = 0$ are real and distinct exactly when the discriminant is strictly positive. With $a = 1$, $b = k$, $c = 3 + k$:

$$\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(3 + k) = k^2 - 4k - 12 = (k - 6)(k + 2).$$

We need $(k-6)(k+2) > 0$. The parabola $\Delta(k) = k^2 - 4k - 12$ opens upwards and has roots $k = -2$ and $k = 6$, so it is positive outside the roots:

| interval | $k < -2$ | $-2 < k < 6$ | $k > 6$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| sign of $(k-6)(k+2)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $+$ |

$$\boxed{\{k \in \mathbb{R} : k < -2 \ \text{or}\ k > 6\}}$$

Check with test values: $k = 7$ gives $x^2 + 7x + 10 = (x+2)(x+5)$, two distinct real roots; $k = -3$ gives $x^2 - 3x = x(x-3)$, two distinct real roots; $k = 0$ gives $x^2 + 3 = 0$, no real roots ($\Delta = -12 < 0$). At $k = -2$ or $k = 6$ the roots are equal ($\Delta = 0$), so these two values are excluded.
